provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the native task, full-width stripes touch the top edge. The output overlays the grid's mirror image across the horizontal midline: each background cell takes the colour of its partner cell at row H-1-r when that partner is not background. Under the D4 convention (reverse each row first, then rotate clockwise d4%4 times), reversing rows leaves a row-mirror unchanged. Each quarter turn swaps rows and columns. So even rotation counts keep the row mirror (partner row H-1-r) and odd counts become a column mirror (partner column W-1-c). Because a mirror is its own reverse, the direction of the stripes (top/bottom/left/right) needs no separate handling. The background role is specialised to the constant palette[0]. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates and implements the overlay with explicit cell loops. It handles rectangular grids of any size.
draft_notes.limitations: Background is fixed to palette[0], matching the constructor, where the canvas is colour 0 and stripe colours come from random_color (assumed non-zero). If a stripe used the background colour, that stripe would be indistinguishable from background and would not be mirrored, which matches the archived solver's behaviour. The stripe stack (at most 4) never reaches the midline of the 10-long axis, so mirrored cells never conflict with existing stripes. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule; I found no contradictions. I have not run any tests.
